relevant_block.original_bytes:
-- testing clearing of dead elements from tables
  collectgarbage("stop")   -- stop GC
  local a = {[{}] = 4, [3] = 0, alo = 1,
             a1234567890123456789012345678901234567890 = 10}

  local t = T.querytab(a)

  for k,_ in pairs(a) do a[k] = undef end
  collectgarbage()   -- restore GC and collect dead fields in 'a'
  for i=0,t-1 do
    local k = querytab(a, i)
    assert(k == nil or type(k) == 'number' or k == 'alo')
  end

rationale: Independently read the pinned locals T block and later insertion refusal sweep, native table_query, the owned collector marking/Clear_Weak phases and Tables.Rebuild/Remember_Free. The first native query result is private array capacity, not logical table membership or total hash storage. The retained native diagnostic reports0,4,0 for this construction, so its subsequent0..t-1 loop executes zero iterations and establishes no hash-node safety coverage in that captured run. Private C array/hash geometry and dead-node representation can be replaced by actual Ada storage safety checks, while public membership, collection/liveness and allocation-refusal behavior remain mandatory. No fabricated C geometry, zero-loop shortcut or removal of public GC/recovery obligations is accepted.
source_findings: table_query returns asize, allocsizenode and lenhint in size mode; its indexed branch exposes actual private C array/hash nodes.
The original numeric loop uses only the first size result. A zero bound does not inspect any hash node, regardless of the unqualified querytab call inside the body.
Collector propagation ignores keys of nil-valued entries. Clear_Weak clears unreachable collectable keys from nil-valued rows, then calls Rebuild before sweep frees those objects.
Rebuild clears dense/hash indices and rebuilds them from actual rows. Nil keys are not linked; nonnil tombstone keys can remain indexed, and nil-valued rows are queued for reuse.
Remember_Free deliberately permits a revived row to remain in the free list until a later insertion pops it. Free-list/index overlap and a live revived row are not automatically corruption.

The manual requires collection when the only references to an explicitly constructed object are weak. Tracking the original anonymous table key in a weak-value table is a relevant public liveness witness; strings/numbers must not be substituted for that collectable object.
retained_requirements: Retain original if rawget(_G,T) guard, explicit collector stop, exact original four-entry construction, pairs deletion, original full collection and later original insertion-refusal sweep byte-for-byte.
Keep both original anchors required and pending. Permit only an exact independently reviewed equivalent; do not add a source exclusion.
Derive the four-before/zero-after count from actual nonnil table values or public iteration, never Members.Length, array capacity, hash capacity or a hardcoded C representation.
Root no extra strong reference to the original anonymous key across the collection. The public weak-value witness must clear after that key is otherwise unreachable.
Inspect actual Ada member/index/free-list structures. Validate collectable reference membership and tag/object-kind consistency before any pointer dereference or hash operation.
Require index bounds, finite acyclic chains, valid row/link/free-list consistency and unlinked nil-key rows; allow legitimate indexed tombstones and revived free-listed rows.
The checker must observe rather than repair storage, rebuild indices, clear keys, alter GC state, reset the allocator or weaken the following fault campaign.

Focused actual counterparts must exercise live-key survival, deleted-key reclamation and same-table dead-row reuse. The later original refusal sweep uses a new shadowing table and alone does not establish reuse of the first table.
Retain all insertion failure/retry positions, partial-table iteration and final five-entry success. Preserve real public errors, ownership cleanup and allocator balance.
required_next_steps: Implement a test-only actual Ada storage checker and separately named positive/negative safety/liveness/reuse cases.
Bind the exact checker and public weak witness sources to a concrete exact replacement manifest and obtain distinct independent exact-source approval.
Verify unchanged native C baseline and relevant public counterpart behavior; select equivalent bytes only for Ada/upstream-test.
Capture fresh same-head raw execution/type/arity/warning/allocator evidence, then obtain the required contract/envelope/matrix reviews.
Recheck source hashes after any Engine/Foreign pool or test-adapter changes; this feature decision cannot renew different source bytes.
